title: Promise and Vow
premise: Lior Dunmore built a career orchestrating other people's perfect days while quietly dismantling her own capacity for love, ever since the man she almost married vanished eleven years ago. When a misdelivered letter—written by him, postmarked the week he disappeared—arrives at her planning studio, she learns his disappearance was no abandonment but an act of protection tied to her family's stolen inheritance. As she investigates outside the courts, where justice failed her family once before, she and Callum Reave, the letter's author now terminally ill, must decide whether a vow made in youth can survive truth, time, and everything they've become. The novel ends with Lior choosing neither the career nor the past as it was, but a new life built on the person who finally sees her clearly.
about_author: Dominic Thornbury is the pen name of a former estate lawyer who left practice after watching one inheritance case destroy three generations of a single family. He writes romance from a converted chapel in coastal Maine, where he insists every love story deserves a fair trial.

chapters.title: The Weather of Other People's Joy
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She flawlessly executes a lavish wedding while privately numb to all of it, revealing her rule: love stays in the past tense. A junior planner asks why she never attends the receptions; Lior deflects. Emotional beat: competent isolation, the armor of professionalism shown in exquisite detail.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Sorting a deceased client's estate boxes, she finds a letter addressed to her, written by Callum Reave, postmarked the week he vanished. She doesn't open it. Emotional beat: the past knocking, her hands shaking over paper she can't yet face.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At 3 a.m. she reads it: Callum didn't leave—he was driven out, and he names her late father's business partner as the reason. The letter ends mid-sentence. Emotional beat: vertigo; the tidy story of her heartbreak collapses.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Supposed to Be Findable
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. In a coastal town two hours away, Callum lives deliberately small, managing a boatyard, hiding from the partner's reach. He receives a call that the partner is dead—and that his own diagnosis gives him months. Emotional beat: grief and strange liberation arriving together.

chapters.title: Dunmore & Daughters
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She digs into her father's old files and finds the family event-planning firm was sold under duress after his death—the inheritance theme surfaces. Her mother refuses to discuss it. Emotional beat: anger kindling into purpose.

chapters.title: Two Hours North
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She drives to find Callum unannounced and watches him across the boatyard before speaking. Their reunion is wary, unfinished sentences everywhere. Emotional beat: recognition that outlasts resentment—but also the shock of how ill he looks.

chapters.title: The Terms of His Silence
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He explains: the partner threatened to frame him for financial fraud unless he disappeared, severing Lior from both him and her inheritance. He took the deal to protect her. Emotional beat: devotion revealed as sacrifice, and her fury that he chose for her.

chapters.title: Evidence Without a Courtroom
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternate. They inventory what proof remains: forged signatures, a coerced witness, a safe-deposit key. Statutes have expired; legal justice is closed. Emotional beat: the pivot to justice outside the law—truth as its own restitution.

chapters.title: The Partner's Widow
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She approaches the widow, Marguerite, under the guise of planning a memorial. Marguerite knows more than she lets on and tests Lior sharply. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Lior using her professional mask as a weapon for the first time.

chapters.title: A Wedding She Almost Believes In
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Back home, she plans a couple's tiny backyard wedding—no spectacle, just vows—and feels something crack open in her. She calls Callum that night and they talk until dawn. Emotional beat: thawing; hope re-entering like a cautious guest.

chapters.title: The Safe-Deposit Key
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He retrieves documents hidden eleven years ago: originals proving the fraud, plus a second letter he never sent. Reading his younger self's words, he decides Lior deserves the whole truth, even the parts that shame him. Emotional beat: courage costing something real.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Bargain
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Marguerite admits she suspected her husband and offers the household ledgers—if Lior publicly frames the memorial as reconciliation, not accusation. Lior must weigh dignity against evidence. Emotional beat: moral compromise, chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He hides a hospital stay from Lior; she finds out through his sister and confronts him. Old patterns repeat—he protects by concealing, she rages at being managed. Emotional beat: the central wound reopened; near-rupture.

chapters.title: The Memorial
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She stages the memorial flawlessly while slipping copies of the ledgers to a journalist ally. Marguerite, watching, gives a nearly imperceptible nod. Emotional beat: Lior weaponizing grace; the investigation goes public.

chapters.title: Print Run
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The exposé lands; the town splits; Lior's mother finally breaks silence and confirms what she suspected for years, asking forgiveness for staying quiet. Emotional beat: family reckoning; grief and vindication tangled together.

chapters.title: The Firm Comes Calling
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A luxury brand offers to buy her studio at a price that would secure her forever—contingent on distancing herself from the scandal. Her career, the thing that saved everything, demands invisibility again. Emotional beat: the true choice sharpening.

chapters.title: What Time Is Doing
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. His decline accelerates; he begins putting affairs in order and drafts a will returning his share of the old firm's proceeds to Lior. He writes a third letter—this one meant to be read. Emotional beat: tenderness under deadline; mortality as clarity.

chapters.title: The Question She Never Asked
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She asks Callum directly why he never came back once the threat eased. His answer—that he assumed she'd built a life better without him—devastates them both. Emotional beat: the cost of noble assumptions; honest grief at last.

chapters.title: Vow
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. In the boatyard at dusk, Callum asks nothing and offers everything; Lior proposes instead—not marriage, but a vow: whatever time remains, they spend it seen. Emotional beat: climax of the heart; commitment without guarantee.

chapters.title: Restitution
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She declines the buyout, signs the studio over to her junior planners as a cooperative, and publishes the full account herself, naming her father's honor restored. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined—not money, but truth passed down.

chapters.title: The Last Good Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Autumn by the water: small days, treatments, laughter, a wedding they attend as guests and actually enjoy. Callum grows weaker; neither pretends otherwise. Emotional beat: bittersweet fullness; love fully present tense at last.

chapters.title: Promise
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, closing. After Callum's death, she opens the third letter—it asks her to live loudly, visibly, loved. One year later she stands at a stranger's wedding not as staff but as witness, wearing his ring on a chain. Emotional beat: resolution; the promise kept, the vow enduring beyond its maker.
